findings.claim: The live SYNAPSE WS bridge is NOT reachable, despite a fresh sidecar advertising it. ~/.synapse/bridge.json is current (pid 61208, port 9999, ts today) and port 9999 is open, but 9/9 WebSocket upgrade attempts returned `InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 400` and 4/4 plain HTTP paths returned 404. Something HTTP-ish holds the port and does not serve the SYNAPSE transport. The SessionStart hook reported 'bridge connected'.

D1-union LOP coverage is degenerate by construction: verified_connectivity_22.0.368.json holds all 218 live Lop types, so D1 = 218/218 = 100% and carries zero information. Any 'we are at 100% LOP coverage' claim sourced from D1 is vacuous.

The relay's '39 of 218 = 18%' has no producing script, no artifact and no U.6 record anywhere in the tree - the only two repo-wide occurrences are inside the relay document itself. The live-probed honest number is 40/218 = 18.3% (D2 union D3), so the prose was approximately right and entirely unsourced.

COPs are effectively ungrounded: 6.2% of 384 live Cop types and 13.6% of 169 Cop2 types carry any emission grounding, and ZERO carry semantic grounding. H22's centre of mass moved into Copernicus and SYNAPSE's grounding did not follow.

Bare type-name emission is ambiguous for 42% of the corpus: 41 of 97 emitted names resolve in 2+ node categories; `null` and `subnet` resolve in all 10. The emission corpus records no category axis, so every coverage number computed from it before this leg was unfalsifiable.

SYNAPSE emits two DEPRECATED LOP types: `karma` and `karmarenderproperties` are both present_lop with deprecated()==true on 22.0.368 - the only 2 deprecated LOPs on the build - and karmarenderproperties is emitted in >=11 places. Not phantom; decaying.
`mtlxstandard_surface` is present in the semantic knowledge artifact lop_solaris_knowledge_22.json but is NOT a live LOP type on 22.0.368 - one poisoned semantic entry.

The '37 vs 196' connectivity contest is a version artifact, and both figures are wrong for H22. H22 has 218 Lop entries (201 with input_labels); the 36-entry figure is the H21.0.671 artifact. Separately, verified_connectivity_H22.json is MALFORMED - it has no `entries` key at all (KeyError).

No grounding/coverage check function exists for either context. The relay's named oracles `lop_emission_grounded` and `no_phantom_api` do not exist; emitted_node_types.json has exactly ONE consumer in checks.py (check_no_rigging_drift, :340) and it only phrase-scans for rigging drift - it never grounds types against a live catalogue.

The 'four confirmed-dead createNode literals' are not substantiated as four literals. Two interpolated geo types are dead (grid, font - emitted via f-string at planner.py:648, invisible to the extractor by design); four ORDER-TABLE entries are dead (merge::2.0, graft, graft::2.0, switchif at handlers_usd.py:1599-1609) but those are frozenset members that never create anything - they mis-classify ordering.

The RAG corpus carries 15 phantom light createNode sites (rectlight/spherelight/disk/cylinder - all absent from the 218) entirely outside the emission gate, re-teaching phantoms via knowledge_lookup and scout. Code/corpus divergence class.
COP parm harvesting is fully instantiation-free: nt.parmTemplateGroup().entriesWithoutFolders() succeeded on all 553 types across both categories with zero fallbacks and zero probe errors.

for_ruling.question: L1 delivered the census; gap CLOSURE is gate-REFUSED (C.0 ratified:false). Flip the gate now, or close gaps in a later run?
options: Flip C.0 and close the top-5 in a follow-on leg
Leave frozen - the census is the deliverable, closure is separate work
Flip C.0 AND re-ratify the H21-vintage catalogues C.1-C.6 depend on
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 3, but sequenced. The census now exists on H22 truth; C.1-C.6 are still armed off an H21 catalogue for an uninstalled build. Flipping C.0 alone would close gaps against a stale capability base. Re-ratify the catalogues first, then flip.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Medium. COPs are 6.2% grounded on the build where Copernicus is the centre of mass - every day of delay is a day the emission corpus mis-teaches COP work.

for_ruling.question: Which grounded-coverage denominator is canonical? All three are now computed, not asserted.
options: D2 literal-emission (31/218, 14.2%) - what SYNAPSE actually emits
D2 union D3 (40/218, 18.3%) - the honest composite
for_ruling.recommendation: D2 union D3 = 18.3%, and RETIRE D1 entirely. D1 is 100% by construction because the connectivity artifact contains the whole live catalogue - it is not a contested number, it is a vacuous one. Any doc quoting a single LOP coverage % should quote 18.3% with its basis named.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: High for governance. Three defensible numbers currently circulate and the relay quoted a fourth with no producer.

for_ruling.question: Which COP category is SYNAPSE's target surface? `Cop` has 384 types, `Cop2` has 169. Both are live on 22.0.368.
options: Cop (384) - the Copernicus surface, H22's centre of mass
Cop2 (169) - the legacy surface, where SYNAPSE's existing 17 handler literals mostly live
for_ruling.recommendation: Cop as the target, Cop2 as maintenance-only. But this is genuinely a product call - it decides where the next year of COP work goes, and presumption is not a ruling.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: High. It gates every COP gap-closure decision that follows from this census.

for_ruling.question: SYNAPSE emits two DEPRECATED LOP types (karma, karmarenderproperties - the only two deprecated LOPs on the build), karmarenderproperties in >=11 places. Remediation is gap-closure, which this leg's gate REFUSES.
options: Flip the gate and migrate the emissions now
Deposit as a ratified:false candidate and migrate after the C.0 ruling
Accept - deprecated is not removed, it still works
for_ruling.recommendation: Deposit as a candidate. Deprecated-but-live is a decay clock, not a fire - but it is exactly the class of thing that becomes a phantom at the next major, and SYNAPSE has been burned by that before.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Low now, high at the next Houdini major.

for_ruling.question: There is no grounding CHECK function for either context - emitted_node_types.json's only consumer is a rigging phrase-scan. Should a real grounding gate be authored?
options: Author check_lop_emission_grounded + check_cop_emission_grounded against the live catalogues
Extend check_phantom_clean to cover emission types
for_ruling.recommendation: Author both. The two halves already exist - harvest_lop_catalog.py is a one-symbol swap from a COP harvester, and the extractor is category-agnostic. The missing piece is only the intersection step, and without it every coverage number in this project is prose.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: High. This is the machinery whose absence let an unsourced 18% sit in a CTO relay document.
